准 can mark a status corresponding to, but not fully the same as, a named rank. In 准教授 じゅんきょうじゅ, it helps name the established rank associate professor. Do not interpret it as a literal half-professor or a trainee awaiting automatic promotion.
Another branch concerns approval: 批准 ひじゅん means ratification. Not every compound containing 准 is an associate rank.

Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology: picture the bird-shaped 隹 beside the two marks of 冫 as a bird standing beside a rank sign. This is an invented memory scene, not an explanation of the character's historical formation.

準 shares ジュン and has related meanings, but its shape has 氵 at the upper left and 十 below. 准 has two left-hand 冫 marks and no lower 十.

The spellings are not freely interchangeable in modern words: learn 準備 じゅんび (preparation), 基準 きじゅん (standard), and 批准 ひじゅん (ratification) as written. JMdict also recognizes 準教授 じゅんきょうじゅ; the current Japanese university title taught here is 准教授.
For look-alikes, 集 has 木 below 隹, 進 has 辶, and 難 has a different, dense left-hand block. Their meanings are not associate rank or approval.

准教授 じゅんきょうじゅ — associate professor

准教授 names an associate professor. In the Japanese university system, this is an established academic rank below 教授 きょうじゅ (professor), with teaching and research responsibilities. It does not mean a professor's personal helper.
彼女は大学の准教授です。 (かのじょはだいがくのじゅんきょうじゅです。) — She is an associate professor at a university.
田中准教授の講義を聞きました。 (たなかじゅんきょうじゅのこうぎをききました。) — I listened to Associate Professor Tanaka's lecture.
The second example places the rank after a name. For respectful direct address, 田中先生 (たなかせんせい) can be appropriate; 先生 is not itself a statement of this particular academic rank.

准 modifies the rank head 教授, marking the associate rank. Within 教授, 教 contributes teaching and 授 contributes imparting knowledge. The on-readings are ジュン + キョウ + ジュ. Learn the whole institutional title rather than translating it as "half a professor."
助教授 じょきょうじゅ is the former Japanese title replaced by 准教授 in April 2007. It remains relevant when reading older documents.
助教 じょきょう, often translated "assistant professor," is a separate rank, not an abbreviation of 准教授.
助手 じょしゅ means assistant and has its own academic uses. It does not by itself identify someone as a 准教授.
教授 きょうじゅ names the professor rank; 先生 せんせい is a broader designation or respectful form of address.
These are role and title comparisons, not strict antonyms.

准教授 is a rank noun, not a verb meaning "work as an associate professor." Use 准教授です (じゅんきょうじゅです) to state the role. The separate teaching/instruction sense of 教授する does not license 准教授する for having this job.

The English label "associate professor" is useful, but rank systems and employment conditions differ between countries and institutions. Do not assume an exact international equivalence or an automatic future promotion. JMdict also lists the spelling 準教授 with the same reading; 准教授 is the current Japanese university title used here.
